title: Find the trend — laboratory turnaround
brief:
The laboratory started a new sample-transport run to cut **turnaround time** (minutes; lower is better). The chart shows 14 weeks, median dashed.

Using the **trend rule** — five or more consecutive points all moving in the same direction — click the points that make up the trend.

(Keyboard users: Tab into the chart, arrow keys to move, Enter to select.)

task.stem: Click each point that is part of the trend (the run of consecutive points all moving the same way). Submit when you have the full trend selected.

debrief.correct: Spotted. Weeks 5–10 fall every single week — 175 → 160 → 148 → 135 → 120 → 108 — that is **six** consecutive decreasing points, which meets the trend rule (five or more). The run clearly starts at week 5 (week 4 → week 5 drops after a rise) and ends at week 10 (the line flattens after). A falling trend in turnaround time is improvement.
debrief.wrong: The trend rule: **five or more consecutive points all moving one way.** Find the unbroken descent — weeks 5 to 10 fall every week (175 → 160 → 148 → 135 → 120 → 108). The early wobble (weeks 1–4) and the plateau after week 10 are not part of the trend. Judge the *direction* of each step, not the height of the points.
debrief.rule_cited: Trend rule — Provost & Murray (2nd ed.), IHI QI 104. Call it at the fifth consecutive step; do not wait for the slope to flatten.
